speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing neck and arm pain, paresthesias, and muscle weakness. To better understand your condition, could you please describe where exactly the pain radiates and if these symptoms have been getting worse over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy with Radiculopathy. The patient's age, chronic burning neck/arm pain, progressive bilateral hand weakness, and paresthesias are classic for cervical spine degeneration. The one-year history and recent acceleration suggest disc herniation or osteophyte formation compressing the spinal cord and nerve roots. Given his comorbidities and trauma history, imaging is critical to confirm the level and severity of compression. REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical_Spine_MRI.
